rationale:
Evidence: iteration 6 is the best design so far (score 696.6). Oval finishes 20 of 20 (mean 1.98 s, max_error 0.0095). S-bend finishes 20 of 20 (mean 2.42 s, steering_oscillation 0.33). Slalom still never finishes (0 of 20, progress 0.47, 1.25 line-loss events per run), so it is the main source of lost score. Across iterations 4 to 6, each step up in kp with a matching step up in kd (4.0/0.6, 4.5/0.8, 4.8/0.9) cut max_error and line losses on s-bend and raised slalom progress, with no oval regression. The diagnosis is that slalom is limited by slow response to rapid direction changes, not by jitter. Oval steering_oscillation (0.23) and s-bend (0.33) still have headroom.

Changes, controller only, geometry unchanged so the effect is isolated: (1) kp 4.8 to 5.0 for more steering authority on fast alternating bends. (2) kd 0.9 to 1.0 to keep the extra proportional gain damped; iteration 2 showed kp 5 with kd 0.3 overshoots, so the damping ratio should be kept at or above the level that worked at kp 4.8. (3) ki 0.5, base_speed 1.3 and line_loss last_direction are unchanged. ki is removing the motor-mismatch bias, and base_speed 1.3 keeps s-bend inside the 3 s limit (about 2.4 s now).

Expected result: slalom progress rises above 0.5 and the first slalom completions appear. Oval stays at 20 of 20 and s-bend completions hold at 100%. Hypotheses: (a) kd 1.0 keeps oval and s-bend steering_oscillation at or below about 0.35 despite the higher kp, so kd is damping rather than adding lag. (b) If oval completion drops or oval steering_oscillation exceeds 0.35, kp 5.0 is too aggressive and should return to 4.8. Sensor coverage (line losses on slalom) is the next suspect if progress stalls near 0.5; a wider sensor footprint would be the next geometry test. Measurements wanted: completion and completion_time by track, progress and max_error on slalom (where the robot leaves the line), line_loss_events and rms_error (effect of kp), and steering_oscillation (effect of kd).
